notes: Frozen, EXTERNAL-reference relationship facts for War and Peace (pg2600) — never text-derived, never fitted to the engine's output. This is a scoring TARGET, same role as span-golden.json/memory-golden.json: the number that matters is how much of this the engine's own machinery (admitCast/presenceBySentence/buildCoOccurrenceEdges/classifyEdges in relationship-graph.js) recovers, run cold against priors/coref/war-and-peace.json + priors/lexicon/en-relations.json. Nobody should ever edit the graph output to match this file — only the engine's discovery/typing logic, scored by scripts/score-relationship-golden.mjs.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_War_and_Peace_characters (fetched 2026-07-29). An encyclopedia summary is itself a set of ASSERTIONS about the text, not a ground truth external to it — it is used here only because it is independent of the extraction pipeline being scored, not because it is infallible. Where a fact could not be located in the actual pg2600 text on a quick check, that is noted rather than assumed.

`referentGap: true` marks a fact whose referent is NOT in priors/coref/war-and-peace.json's current cast (Lise/Liza Bolkónskaya, young Nikólai/Nikólenka Bolkonsky, Count Kiríll Bezúkhov, Márya Ivánovna Dólokhova) — the scorer must report these as a missing-referent gap, never silently skip them, and never as a false 'miss' on the edge-detection logic.

`relation` values are the external vocabulary this golden speaks in; scripts/score-relationship-golden.mjs owns the (documented, revisable) mapping from these onto the engine's current lexicon categories (priors/lexicon/en-relations.json) and stated-relation verbs — that mapping is expected to evolve as the lexicon does, independent of this file.
